The named limiter is missing a key:
```php
return Limit::perMinute(3)->by($request->ip());
```
Without `by(...)`, every `/request-otp` request shares one global bucket, so three requests from any visitor exhaust the limit for everyone.
Use Laravel’s `$request->ip()` rather than reading `X-Forwarded-For` directly. Configure trusted proxies only for the actual production proxy/load balancer; otherwise client-supplied forwarding headers must not influence the IP used for throttling. Add tests proving separate clients have separate buckets and spoofed headers cannot bypass the limit.
<diagnosis>
The `otp` limiter defines only `perMinute(3)` and no request-specific key, causing Laravel to use one shared rate-limit bucket for all visitors. A single visitor’s three requests therefore throttle the entire endpoint. Fix it with `Limit::perMinute(3)->by($request->ip())`, and ensure proxy trust is restricted to known infrastructure so arbitrary `X-Forwarded-For` headers cannot change the throttling identity or bypass the limit.
</diagnosis>
